summary: G. C. Nayak (1935–2021) worked in philosophy and Indology. He served as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study and as a Senior Fellow at the Indian Council of Philosophical Research in 1996.

G. Clinton Godart specializes in Japanology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Chicago under James Edward Ketelaar, held postdoctoral posts at Cambridge and the Needham Research Institute, and taught at USC and Hokkaido University.
G. K. Jenkins (1918–2005) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Bloxham School, he spent his career at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera (1899–1973) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede, he taught at Ceylon University College and the University of Ceylon.

G. Thomas Tanselle (b. 1934) studied at Yale University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978) and Columbia University (~1978–2006), and served as vice president of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation from 1978 to 2006.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.

Gadjin Nagao (1907–2005) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Susumu Yamaguchi and Ryotai Hani, and held Kyoto University's Chair of Buddhist Studies from 1935 to 1971.

Gail Hinich Sutherland is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago under advisers Carol Bolon and Wendy Doniger, and also studied under traditional teacher Virendra Singh.

Galsan Gomboev (1822–1863) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and taught Mongolian at Saint Petersburg State University from 1855 to 1863.

Gananath Obeyesekere (1930–2025) was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Ceylon and University of Washington, and held posts at Ceylon, Washington, UC San Diego, and Princeton University (1980–2000).

Ganesh Prasad (1876–1935) studied at the universities of Allahabad and Calcutta. He served as a department head at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1917–1923) and the University of Calcutta (~1914–1935).

Ganganatha Jha (1872–1941) was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Muir Central College and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (1923–1932).
Gangs zhun is a Tibetologist who studied at Qinghai Nationalities Normal College and earned a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under Alak Dorzhi Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.Phil. at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008) and also studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa.
Garab Dorje Rinpoche (b. 1967) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy (1794–1878) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Collège de France under Silvestre de Sacy and François-Daniel Kieffer, and held the chair of Indian languages at INALCO from ~1828 to 1878.

Gareth Fisher works in Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (2006) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham (b. 1948) works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and UBC under Ashok Narhar Aklujkar, later lecturing in Tibetan language at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb (b. 1950) is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty appointments at Harvard University, Columbia University, and the University of Chicago, where he became Anupama and Guru Ramakrishnan Professor Emeritus.

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He was mentored by Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Daud Rahbar, and served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at Holy Cross.
